highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has officially launched Claude Opus 5, now the default Opus model with a massive 1M token context window and fast mode pricing at $10/$50 per million tokens. This is a significant upgrade for developers working on large codebases or long agentic sessions in Claude Code. If you're on VS Code with Claude Code, you can access it via the model identifier `claude-opus-5`.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.219: Opus 5 Default, Sandbox Network Allowlist, and DirectoryAdded Hook
highlights.summary: Version 2.1.219 adds Claude Opus 5 as the default Opus model directly in Claude Code, so you'll automatically benefit from the larger context window without changing settings. A new `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` setting lets you lock down which hosts sandboxed commands can reach, improving security for automated workflows. The new `DirectoryAdded` hook gives advanced users a trigger point when directories are added to the session.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.218: /code-review Now Runs as Background Subagent
highlights.summary: The `/code-review` slash command has been upgraded to run as a background subagent, meaning it no longer clutters your active conversation with review output. This keeps your main chat focused on your current task while the review happens in parallel. Stacked slash commands will now correctly use the review target, fixing a common workflow annoyance.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.216: Sandbox Filesystem Toggle and Quadratic Slowdown Fix
highlights.summary: A critical performance bug has been fixed where long sessions experienced multi-second stalls because message normalization cost grew quadratically with the number of conversation turns — upgrading should make long coding sessions noticeably snappier. The new `sandbox.filesystem.disabled` setting lets you skip filesystem isolation while still keeping network egress controls active, useful when you need file access freedom but still want network security. If you've ever noticed Claude Code slowing down near the end of a long session, this update is a must-have.

highlights.title: Anthropic Runs Large-Scale Code Migrations with Claude Code
highlights.summary: Anthropic has published a case study detailing how they use Claude Code internally to perform large-scale codebase migrations, offering a rare look at how AI-assisted refactoring works at production scale. This is valuable reading for developers considering using Claude Code for legacy code modernization or cross-framework migrations. The post likely includes practical patterns you can adapt for your own migration projects.

highlights.title: Cognikernel: Local Persistent Memory for AI Coding Assistants
highlights.summary: Cognikernel is an open-source tool that gives Claude Code and similar AI assistants persistent memory across sessions, so architectural decisions and project context aren't lost when you start a new chat. Instead of manually maintaining a `CLAUDE.md` file, Cognikernel stores and retrieves relevant context automatically. This is especially useful for long-running projects where you need Claude to remember decisions made days or weeks ago.

highlights.title: Complete 60-Minute Claude Code Masterclass (Chinese, with Full Documentation)
highlights.summary: This comprehensive Bilibili tutorial covers Claude Code from initial installation all the way through advanced usage patterns in a single 60-minute session, accompanied by full written documentation. The creator spent three weeks preparing the material, making it one of the most thorough Chinese-language resources available for Claude Code learners. Even if you don't speak Chinese, the linked Feishu documentation from the beginner-level companion video may contain useful structured notes.

highlights.title: Claude Code Tutorial for Non-Coders
highlights.summary: This YouTube tutorial is specifically designed for people without a coding background who want to start using Claude Code, making it one of the most accessible entry points for non-technical users. It walks through the core concepts and workflows needed to get productive without assuming prior programming knowledge. If you've been hesitant to try Claude Code because you're not a developer, this video is the right starting point.

tips_of_the_day: After upgrading to Claude Code v2.1.216+, start a fresh session for long refactoring tasks — the quadratic slowdown fix means you'll no longer hit multi-second stalls, but only new sessions benefit from the optimized message normalization.

Use `/code-review` at the end of a feature branch before merging: since v2.1.218 it runs as a background subagent, so you can keep working on your next task in the same conversation while the review completes in parallel.

Create a `cognikernel` or structured `CLAUDE.md` file at the root of every project and document key architectural decisions after each session — even one or two bullet points per session compounds into invaluable context that prevents Claude from suggesting changes that contradict past decisions.
